6_analysis.falsification_postmortem: The card pre-registered outcome (a) and band (c) fired: nRMSE 0.3117986 against a band-(a) ceiling of 0.290216, i.e. the prediction missed by 0.0216 nRMSE (1.336 skill = 0.818 of one floor above the edge) while the deciding rel-vs-MSE degradation itself is +2.9696 skill = 1.818 floors, above the certified floor. WHY THE PREDICTION WAS WRONG, mechanism-level: part 4 inherited B1's M2, and B1's M2 was derived from an exact but INCOMPLETE reduction. B1 F1 proved that L_lambda(p, y) depends only on the two per-sample scalars (r, cos) -- a genuine result, verified to 4e-14 -- and M2 then reasoned entirely inside that reduction: at lambda=1 the origin stationary point disappears, the escape drive is the finite constant 2(1-alpha), and the perverse-descent region is algebraically empty. All of that is TRUE and was CONFIRMED here (F5: frac_perverse 0.00, g_median 0.988, 93.5% of the collapse recovered). The reduction's blind spot is that it is a SINGLE-SAMPLE object: it describes the loss surface for one (p, y) pair and integrates out the fact that one shared network is fitted to 100 samples SIMULTANEOUSLY. Per-sample normalization changes the objective in two places -- the per-sample loss SHAPE (which the reduction sees, and which is harmless at lambda=1) and the BETWEEN-SAMPLE WEIGHTING w ~ 1/||y||^2 (which the reduction cannot see at all, because it never has two samples in scope). B1 had actually MEASURED that second channel -- F5's top-decile weight share 0.691, F13's effective sample fraction 0.163, and M6's whole design rule are about it -- but M2 wrote the prediction from the geometry finding rather than from the weighting finding, and the two disagreed. The weighting channel is worth 1.818 floors on this dataset and it was the entire content of the miss. A secondary reason the miss was inevitable at the band level: part 4's interval [0.24, 0.29] was one floor wide around the MSE comparator, so ANY non-zero cost of the weighting channel above 1.0 floors had to land outside it -- the prediction had no room for a second mechanism it did not believe in. What this does NOT falsify: the clause's literal FALSIFIED branch (band b, 'normalization is fatal regardless of lambda') is itself refuted (F5), and B1's M1/M6(3) -- lambda <= 1 -- stand as measured.

The arm that gets the physics of amplitude right is the arm the metric punishes.

The worst sample (1.664, ||y|| = the split minimum 2.276) is not a blow-up or a NaN: it is a full-amplitude, correctly-textured, wrongly-registered spinodal pattern. Two uncorrelated full-amplitude patterns differ by more than one of them -- rel^2 = 1 + g^2 - 2 g cos = 2.77 with g 1.62, cos 0.26.
The rel arm has FEWER amplitude-collapsed samples than the MSE arm (1 vs 6 with g < 0.5) and a worse score. 'Amplitude collapse count' and 'score' point in opposite directions here.

An oracle per-sample rescale of the SAME predictions (0.31180 -> 0.28099) crosses the card's band-(a) edge (0.290216). The band that fired is a property of the amplitude calibration, not of the learned representation: the same network, rescaled, would have confirmed B1's M2.
